name: Meen Varuthathu
subtitle: chilli-and-pepper crusted fish shallow fried in coconut oil until the edges blister

ingredients.qty: 600g, 4 steaks or whole small fish, slashed

prepNotes: Pat the fish bone dry with paper towel and cut two deep slashes into each side, right down to the bone. Wet fish will never crisp.
Mix the chilli powders, turmeric, pepper, ginger, garlic, lemon juice and salt into a thick paste with 1 tbsp water and rub it into the slashes.
Marinate 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 2 hours refrigerated. Longer than that and the lemon starts to cook the flesh.

steps.text: Bring the marinated fish back to room temperature for 15 minutes if it has been in the fridge.
Dust each piece lightly with rice flour on both sides and shake off the excess.
steps.tip: A thin film only. A thick coat turns pasty in the pan.

steps.text: Heat the coconut oil in a heavy tawa over medium-high until a pinch of flour dropped in sizzles instantly.
Slide in the fish, laying it away from you, and do not touch it for 4 minutes.
steps.tip: Moving it early tears the crust off. Wait until it releases on its own.

steps.text: Turn once and fry the second side 3-4 minutes until the crust is deep brick red and the flesh at the slash is opaque.
Throw the curry leaves into the hot oil around the fish for the last 30 seconds until they crisp.
steps.tip: Stand back — wet leaves in hot oil spit hard.

steps.text: Lift onto a plate, scatter the crisped leaves over, and serve within minutes with rice and a wedge of lemon.

storage: Eat hot from the pan. Leftovers keep 1 day refrigerated; re-crisp in a dry hot pan for 2 minutes a side rather than reheating in a microwave.
